## Goal

Evaluate the rule chosen in the **no-covariate half-A exploration**, using the
covariate-adjusted models on **the same half-B counties**. Reuse the diagnostic
and numeric cutoff from `analysis/3.1a.4_heldout_decision.yml` unchanged; do not explore
other diagnostics or cutoffs here. Models were fit on all counties. This document
loads only the physically separate covariate half-B input and stops if the decision
file is missing or invalid. It neither loads nor reruns half-A analysis.

Prepare the covariate inputs using the added chunk in 3c.0, or the standalone
shared preparation command documented in this folder's README. No model fit is
run by this document. The original `data/derived/heldout/county_assignment.rds` and its
hash are checked at load time; no new split is generated.

```{r setup}
# Validate the fixed choice before opening any half-B diagnostic rows.
root<-normalizePath(getwd())
while(!file.exists(file.path(root,'R/fe.r'))) {
 parent<-dirname(root); if(parent==root) stop('Repository not found'); root<-parent
}
source(file.path(root,'R/heldout_analysis.R'))
decision<-read_decision(root)
obj<-load_heldout_half(root,'B', input_dir=file.path(root,'data/derived/heldout/with_covariates'))
d<-derive_heldout(obj$rows); z<-d$rows
out<-file.path(root,'_output/heldout/with_covariates/confirmation');dir.create(out,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
assignment<-readRDS(file.path(root,'data/derived/heldout/county_assignment.rds'))
```

## Recorded choice and fixed split

Diagnostic: **`r decision$diagnostic`**. Cutoff: **`r decision$cutoff`**.
Date: `r as.character(decision$date)`. Rationale: `r decision$rationale`.
Decision file MD5: `r decision$md5`.

The **original no-covariate** county split uses seed **`r unique(assignment$split_seed)`**, stratified into
quintiles of mean pre-period expected count from saved **no-covariate** main TWFE MAR fits.
Within each fit the available pre-period expected counts are averaged; those
means are averaged across replications. County ID breaks size ties. A seeded
shuffle balances A/B within each quintile; missing size uses a separate stratum.
The assignment is fixed and saved before exploration. Within-simulation
statistics and top-decile outcomes are defined within B alone.

There are **`r nrow(obj$manifest)` of `r obj$expected_groups`** expected checkpoints.
An incomplete snapshot gives provisional confirmation only. No other candidate
rules are compared here and no choice is revised based on B. The recorded rule
is applied separately to each covariate model; their retained county samples can
differ. All primary and explanatory targets below come from the covariate main
fits, and held-out diagnostics come from their covariate backdated fits.

```{r counts}
# Report B availability and the replication counts underlying explanatory county averages.
fwrite(d$averages,file.path(out,'county_average_targets.csv'))
availability<-z[,.(rows=.N,counties=uniqueN(id),simulations=uniqueN(sim),
 usable_rule=sum(is.finite(get(decision$diagnostic)))),by=.(scenario,model)]
fwrite(availability,file.path(out,'availability.csv'));knitr::kable(availability)
knitr::kable(d$averages[,.(counties=.N,min_raw_R=min(n_average_raw),median_raw_R=median(n_average_raw),
 max_raw_R=max(n_average_raw),zero_raw_R=sum(n_average_raw==0),
 median_standardized_R=median(n_average_standardized)),by=.(scenario,model)])
fwrite(obj$manifest,file.path(out,'input_manifest.csv'))
yaml::write_yaml(decision,file.path(out,'evaluated_decision.yml'))
```

## Fixed-rule associations

Primary targets are absolute five-year realized post-period count error and that
error divided by the square root of its predicted mean. Secondary targets average
each of these over finite replications for each county/model/scenario. This is
an explanatory analysis of systematic prediction difficulty; averages include
the evaluated replication and still contain sampling noise. The number of
contributing replications is saved in `county_average_targets.csv`.

Scores are the absolute chosen diagnostic, or `1 - p_two` for predictive mid-p.
Two-sided mid-p is computed from the saved mid-p tails as
`min(1, 2 * min(p_upper, p_lower))`. Spearman correlation and AUC are computed
within B for each simulation. Top-decile labels include ties at the 90th
percentile; AUC gives score ties half credit. Missing or nonpositive denominators
are unavailable. Summaries equally weight simulations with finite statistics.

```{r metrics}
# Evaluate the selected diagnostic only, against realized and explanatory averaged targets.
metrics<-evaluate_diagnostics(z,decision$diagnostic)
fwrite(metrics,file.path(out,'metrics_by_simulation.csv'))
summary<-summarize_metrics(metrics,c('n_valid','spearman','auc'),c('scenario','model','diagnostic','target'))
counts<-metrics[,.(valid_correlation_simulations=sum(is.finite(spearman)),valid_auc_simulations=sum(is.finite(auc))),
 by=.(scenario,model,diagnostic,target)]
summary<-merge(summary,counts,by=c('scenario','model','diagnostic','target'))
fwrite(summary,file.path(out,'metrics_summary.csv'));knitr::kable(summary,digits=3)
```

## Fixed-rule exclusion performance

For `p_two`, exclude values strictly below the cutoff. For all other diagnostics,
exclude absolute values strictly above it. Denominators require a finite diagnostic
and target. Unavailable shares are reported separately. Retained mean error is
compared with the unfiltered mean on that same eligible sample.

```{r cutoffs}
# Apply exactly the recorded cutoff, without exploring alternatives on B.
rules<-data.table(diagnostic=decision$diagnostic,cutoff=decision$cutoff)
cutoffs<-cutoff_performance(z,rules)
fwrite(cutoffs,file.path(out,'cutoffs_by_simulation.csv'))
summary<-summarize_metrics(cutoffs,c('n_eligible','unavailable_share','excluded_share','baseline_error','retained_error','reduction'),
 c('scenario','model','diagnostic','cutoff','target'))
fwrite(summary,file.path(out,'cutoffs_summary.csv'));knitr::kable(summary,digits=3)
```
